jobDescription:

jobDescription:
Overview: Dozee Health AI is a pioneer in Contactless Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), proven to drive transformation at scale. Headquartered in Bengaluru, India, Dozee has emerged as India’s no. 1 RPM Company. We are seeking visionary individuals to help us in this very exciting journey. As a part of our dynamic team, you’ll have the opportunity to collaborate with top healthcare providers in the country, applying AI-powered RPM solutions to tackle some of the most pressing challenges in healthcare
- enhancing staff efficiency, improving patient outcomes, and pioneering the next generation of care models. We're hiring a Supply Chain Lead to own our supply chain end-to-end "Procurement, Manufacturing, and Logistics"
- in a regulated medical device environment. This is a hands-on

ROLE:
you will lead the teams, own processes, budgets and track spends, drive demand planning, and keep every process audit-ready. We're hiring a Supply Chain Lead to own our supply chain end-to-end "Procurement, Manufacturing, and Logistics"
- in a regulated medical device environment. This is a hands-on

ROLE:
you will lead the teams, own processes, budgets and track spends, drive demand planning, and keep every process audit-ready. Key Responsibilities Procurement Demand planning
- lead demand planning in partnership with Sales, translating the sales forecast and pipeline into a material and component procurement plan. Supplier onboarding & quality
- qualify and onboard suppliers via a risk-classified Approved Supplier List (ASL) process; drive incoming quality control (IQC); and negotiate favorable delivery schedules, pricing, and payment / credit terms. Audit documentation & CAPAs
- own supplier management documentation for audits (supplier files, quality agreements, evaluation and re-evaluation records) and raise CAPAs against non-conformances, driving root-cause analysis and effectiveness checks to closure Team management
- lead, prioritize, and mentor the procurement team. Budgets
- prepare and track procurement budgets, monitoring budget vs. actuals and driving cost-savings initiatives. Audits
- participate in inventory audits and QMS audits, keeping procurement records audit-ready at all times. Manufacturing Manufacturing partners
- onboard and manage contract manufacturers / EMS partners end-to-end apart from inhouse manufacturing. Enforce quality control, and negotiate favorable delivery and payment terms in support of production. Efficiency & output
- track manufacturing efficiency and output against plan, resolving bottlenecks between suppliers and the production line. Stock visibility
- build dashboards and reports giving the Sales team real-time visibility into stock levels and availability. COGS
- track COGS for each production cycle and surface variances against standard cost. Team management
- manage the manufacturing team Audits
- participate in inventory audits and QMS audits. Engineering feedback loop
- review field tickets and failure reports, translating recurring issues into structured inputs for the Engineering team to drive design / process improvements. Logistics (Domestic & International) Distribution, imports & exports
- lead the logistics team covering domestic distribution, imports, and exports. 3PL & warehousing
- onboard and manage 3PL partners, evaluate zone-wise utilization, and stand up local / regional warehousing where the network requires it. Cost
- own logistics cost (freight, customs, warehousing) and drive it down against KPIs. ERP tracking
- set up ERP modules for shipment tracking and end-to-end visibility. TATs
- define and maintain shipment turnaround times (TATs) and hold the network accountable to them. Cross-Functional & Systems ERP & dashboards
- set up and administer ERP workflows (IQC gating, NC / CAPA tracking, supplier status, inventory, shipment modules) and build management dashboards for spend, COGS, inventory turns, on-time delivery, and supplier performance. Consolidated budget
- own the consolidated supply chain budget Regulatory audits
- serve as a supply chain point-of-contact in ISO 13485, CE (MDR), and FDA audits, partnering closely with QARA. Requirements 8+ years in supply chain / operations across procurement, manufacturing, and logistics Proven experience managing teams and managing spends / budgets Strong supplier onboarding and negotiation track record (delivery terms, payment / credit terms, quality). Hands-on ERP experience
- setting up or administering procurement, inventory, and logistics modules. Strong analytical skills; comfortable building dashboards and reporting on COGS, inventory, and KPIs. 2. HR Analytics & Data Management Build and maintain HR dashboards (headcount, attrition, hiring funnel, engagement, DEI, cost-to-company) for leadership review. Pull and consolidate data from the HRIS and other people systems to build these dashboards (not responsible for owning or administering the HRIS itself). - enhancing staff efficiency, improving patient outcomes, and pioneering the next generation of care models. Role Overview We are looking for a Firmware Test Engineer with 2-3 years of hands-on experience in firmware or embedded systems, who is passionate about understanding how devices behave in the real world. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy working with real hardware, running systems in long loops, and investigating failures to understand not just what broke, but why. You will work closely with firmware engineers to test device functionality, identify regressions, and improve system reliability. Over time, you will grow into building test automation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) setups, and firmware CI/CD pipelines. If you are a firmware engineer-or come from a related embedded background-and are curious, motivated, and eager to expand your skill set into testing, automation, and reliability engineering, you are welcome to apply. Why This Role Exists As our devices and firmware scale, informal or manual testing is no longer sufficient. Devices must behave correctly not only in ideal conditions, but also across resets, power cycles, degraded communication, and long-running field scenarios. This role exists to ensure that firmware failures are found early, in the lab-not in the field. By investing in firmware test engineering, we aim to improve observability, reduce deployment risk, and increase confidence in every firmware release.
